page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#decision-summary]

## Decision Summary

**Entity Framework Core Migrations** is the sole approved tool for Aurora PostgreSQL schema changes in the Member BC. All migrations are **forward-only** (no automatic rollback scripts), **idempotent**, and applied as a **Kubernetes Job** that runs before pod rollout in each environment. For multi-tenant deployments, a Terraform-automated fan-out applies the migration Job sequentially across all tenant clusters before the new pod version is released.

---
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#context-and-problem-statement]

## Context and Problem Statement

- **Business Context**: The Member BC manages PHI for multiple state tenants, each with a dedicated Aurora PostgreSQL cluster (ADR-APP-005). Schema changes must be applied to all tenant clusters reliably, in order, and without data loss before any new application version processes live member data.
- **Technical Context**: ADR-APP-001 mandates Entity Framework Core (Npgsql) as the ORM. The logical architecture mandates "EF Core migrations run as Kubernetes Job pre-rollout." The multi-tenant data model means a single migration must fan out to N Aurora clusters — one per deployed state tenant — before the rolling pod update proceeds. Without a documented strategy, each developer team member will make independent decisions about tooling, rollback, and fan-out.
- **Problem Statement**: How are database schema changes authored, tested, versioned, applied across N tenant clusters, and rolled back if needed — in a way that satisfies HIPAA change-control requirements and supports zero-downtime deployments?
page_texts.6:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#decision-drivers]

### Decision Drivers

- EF Core is already mandated (ADR-APP-001) — migration authoring tooling is settled
- Multi-tenant topology (ADR-APP-005) requires fan-out to N clusters — must be automated
- Zero-downtime deployments require migrations to be backward-compatible with the running pod version
- HIPAA change-control requirements demand an auditable migration history per tenant cluster
- ArgoCD GitOps (ADR-INFRA-005) is the deployment mechanism — migration Jobs must fit the GitOps model

---
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#migration-tooling]

### Migration Tooling

**Entity Framework Core Migrations** (via `dotnet ef migrations add` / `dotnet ef database update`). No alternative tools (Flyway, Liquibase, raw SQL scripts) are used for the Member BC relational schema. EF Core is the authoritative migration source.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#migration-policy]

### Migration Policy

| Rule | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Forward-only** | No `Down()` migration methods are implemented. Rollback is handled by deploying the previous application version (which is compatible with the current schema — see backward-compatibility rule below). Automatic schema rollback is prohibited — it risks data loss on populated tables. |
| **Backward-compatible** | Every migration must be safe to run while the previous application version is still serving traffic. This means: add columns as nullable first; populate with defaults; add NOT NULL constraint in a follow-on migration at the next release. Drop columns only after the column has been unused for one full release cycle. |
| **Idempotent** | All migrations are generated with `--idempotent` flag for `script` output. The migration runner checks `__EFMigrationsHistory` and skips already-applied migrations. |
| **Single source of truth** | Migration files live in `components/dotnet/src/<concern>/Migrations/`. No hand-edited SQL migration scripts alongside EF migrations. |
| **Naming convention** | EF Core timestamp prefix is preserved: `20260706143022_AddEligibilitySpanIndex.cs`. PR title must reference the migration name. |
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#application-mechanism--kubernetes-job]

### Application Mechanism — Kubernetes Job

Migrations are applied by a dedicated Kubernetes Job that runs as part of the ArgoCD sync wave before the Deployment rollout:

```yaml
# helm/templates/migration-job.yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: mbr-migration-{{ .Release.Revision }}
  annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync
    argocd.argoproj.io/hook-delete-policy: BeforeHookCreation
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: migrator
          image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
          command: ["dotnet", "MMES.CMS.MBR.Migrator.dll"]
          env:
            - name: MMES_DATABASE_URL
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: mbr-aurora-credentials
                  key: connection-string
      restartPolicy: Never
  backoffLimit: 3
```

- The Job uses `argocd.argoproj.io/hook: PreSync` — it must complete successfully before any pod is replaced
- If the Job fails after 3 retries, the ArgoCD sync is aborted; the running pods continue serving with the current schema
- Job completion is verified before the Deployment rollout proceeds (ArgoCD sync wave ordering)
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#multi-tenant-fan-out]

### Multi-Tenant Fan-Out

Each tenant has a dedicated Aurora cluster. The same migration Job manifest is deployed to each tenant's EKS namespace via ArgoCD ApplicationSets:

```yaml
# argocd/applicationset-migration.yaml
generators:
  - list:
      elements:
        - tenant: oh
          cluster: eks-oh.gainwell.internal
        - tenant: oh
          cluster: eks-oh.gainwell.internal
template:
  metadata:
    name: mbr-migration-{{tenant}}
  spec:
    syncPolicy:
      syncOptions:
        - CreateNamespace=true
```

- Migrations are applied **sequentially per tenant** (not in parallel) to limit blast radius
- Terraform automation provisions the ApplicationSet entries when a new state tenant is onboarded — no manual step required
- Each tenant's `__EFMigrationsHistory` table provides an independent audit trail per cluster
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#rollback-strategy]

### Rollback Strategy

Schema rollback is **not automated**. Rollback is achieved by:

1. **Code rollback** (primary): Deploy the previous application image tag via ArgoCD — the previous version is compatible with the current schema because all migrations are backward-compatible
2. **Data fix migration** (if schema change caused data corruption): Author a new forward migration that corrects the data; deploy it as a normal release
3. **Break-glass** (catastrophic failure only): Aurora PITR restore — RTO 4 hours per ADR-INFRA-001; requires Database Engineering approval and produces a compliance incident record

---
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#option-1-flyway--liquibase-rejected]

### Option 1: Flyway / Liquibase (Rejected)

**Pros**: Technology-agnostic; SQL-first; widely used
**Cons**: Introduces a second migration tool alongside EF Core; migration files would diverge from the EF Core model; no benefit over EF Core for a .NET-only codebase; adds operational dependency
page_texts.15:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#option-2-raw-sql-scripts-applied-by-ci-rejected]

### Option 2: Raw SQL Scripts Applied by CI (Rejected)

**Pros**: Full control over SQL; no framework dependency
**Cons**: No migration history tracking; no idempotency guarantee; incompatible with EF Core change tracking; violates ADR-APP-001 (EF Core as ORM)

[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#option-3-ef-core-migrations--kubernetes-job-presync-selected]

### Option 3: EF Core Migrations + Kubernetes Job PreSync (Selected)

See Decision above.

page_texts.18:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#positive]

### Positive

- Single tool for schema and migration — EF Core model and migration files stay in sync
- GitOps-compatible — migration Job is a Kubernetes manifest in the Helm chart; reviewed and audited like any other change
- Automatic fan-out via ArgoCD ApplicationSets — no manual per-tenant deployment steps
- Pre-sync hook ensures schema is always ahead of or equal to the application version
page_texts.19:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#negative]

### Negative

- Forward-only policy requires discipline — breaking schema changes must be staged across two releases
- Fan-out is sequential, not parallel — applying migrations to 10 tenant clusters adds ~10× the migration time to the deployment pipeline
- EF Core migration conflicts (two developers add migrations simultaneously) must be resolved by rebasing migration files
page_texts.20:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#neutral]

### Neutral

- `dotnet ef migrations bundle` produces a self-contained migration executable suitable for the Job container without requiring the full SDK in production images

---
page_texts.21:
[strategy/guidance/application/GUID-APP-DB-001-forward-only-migration-strategy.md#compliance-notes]

## Compliance Notes

- **Security**: Migration Job uses AWS Secrets Manager CSI Driver to inject Aurora credentials (ADR-APP-011); credentials never in environment variables or image layers
- **Regulatory**: `__EFMigrationsHistory` table per tenant cluster provides an auditable, timestamped record of every schema change — satisfies HIPAA change-control requirement; retained with Aurora cluster for 7 years
- **Standards**: Forward-only idempotent migrations align with STD-APP-CFG-001 (configuration management) change management principles

---
